newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S.-style fitness centres muscle into Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-style fitness centres muscle into Hong Kong.

text.p: Wealthy Hong Kong traded pampering for pure sweat on Wednesday with the grand opening of a California-style fitness centre.

American gyms are muscling their way into the Hong Kong fitness market, among them the Ray Wilson California Fitness Center which inaugurated the new health club in Hong Kong's trendy yuppie district of Lan Kwai Fong.

"There are many fitness centres in Hong Kong. There are not that many that cater strictly to pure fitness," said Eric Levine, managing director of California Fitness, referring to beauty programmes such as facials available at other clubs.
The club boasts of "celebrity" members as well as six floors of body-building machinery.
But the battle for the bulging bicep is not the only fight being waged in the industry in Hong Kong, where clubs are pumping aggressive marketing techniques to bring in clientele.
Lean prices are offered to fast joiners who have a chance to win free trips to the United States if they bring a friend.
California Fitness pulled in a big crowd at its grand opening ceremony by inviting Hong Kong's British colonial governor Chris Patten as its guest of honour.
"I am always delighted to welcome any additional facilities in Hong Kong," Patten said with a smile.
The West Coast health club has an East Coast rival -- New York Fitness Center also opened its doors recently.
Relations between the two are so sour that New York Fitness director Anthony Desir declined to be interviewed for an article that would mention California Fitness.
The Hong Kong market seems to have huge growth potential.

Ray Wilson, who attended the inauguration, said only one tenth of a percent of Hong Kong's 6.3 million people are members of a health club compared with about 25 percent in most major states on the West Coast of the United States.
"The fitness movement...will be just as significant and just as overwhelming in Asia as it is in the United States," he said.
"Our goal throughout Asia is to educate the people and to bring it up to 20 or 25 percent of people belonging to fitness centres," Wilson said.
